newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Norilsk drops, other Russian shares off highs.
newsitem.headline: Norilsk drops, other Russian shares off highs.

text.p: Norilsk Nickel dropped 17 percent in late trading on news of a huge rights issue, and late profit-taking on other leading Russian shares, sparked by aggressive Western selling, hacked into early gains on Tuesday, traders said.
But they saw the decline slowing or stabilising in the next few days if the selling eased.

The Russian Trading System 22-share index still managed to squeak in at a record 517.54, off a daily high of 519.19, on $67.0 million total market turnover. The index closed on Tuesday at 516.63, the previous record.

"I think some major player in the West decided to sell -- the market was nervous anyway and was holding on Russian money alone for the second week in a row," said ING Bank trader Oleg Galkin. "Prices are now already fairly low and so today and tomorrow the market ought to correct again and consolidate at these levels."

Traders said telecoms in general and in particular international long-distance carrier Rostelekom, which had been boosted in recent days by Friday's sale of a quarter stake in telecoms holding company Svyazinvest, were hit hardest.

Rostelekom RTKM.RTS sank to $4.95 after closing on Monday at $5.34, but Moscow city telephone company MGTS MGTS.RTS rose to $2.5 after $2.35 previously. Oil company LUKoil LKOH.RTS ticked down to $22.40 from $22.85.

Metals producer Norilsk Nickel NKEL.RTS plummeted about 17 percent to $14.00 from $17.00 on Monday after the company announced it would ask shareholders to approve doubling capital at an extraordinary meeting on September 8.
Traders said investors feared the rights issue could result in a dilution of holdings.
"People don't like increases in charter capital," said Regent European Securities trader Alexander Fonarkov.
Norilsk also announced after the market closed that the rights issue would price shares at 30,000 roubles ($5.17, about one-third of market price before the announcement).
